text:
Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game last week, and the Hurricanes honored him before a 7-4 win over Edmonton, the team that drafted him first overall in 2010. He had two points that night against his old club. Connor McDavid gave him a congratulatory hug, per Cory Lavalette of North State Journal.

It's a fitting milestone for a career that took him through seven teams, a Hart Trophy in 2017-18 and, finally, a Stanley Cup with Carolina last season.

At 35 he plays a smaller role now, about 13 minutes a night, but in those minutes he's terrific. Carolina takes 66% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 with him on the ice, and he scores at 3.06 points per 60, a first-line rate. Evolving-Hockey's numbers caution that his teammates are excellent (96th percentile), which flatters him, but they also had him driving offense at a 91st percentile rate. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man: 9.6 primary shot assists per 60. Ten points in 15 games is a fine way to start the next thousand.
